name: Siouxsie and the Banshees
description:
'''Siouxsie and the Banshees''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|s|u|z|i|_|æ|n|d|_|ð|ə|_|ˈ|b|æ|n|ʃ|i|z}} {{respell|SU|zi|and|the|BAN|shees}}) were a [[British rock]] band formed in London in 1976 by vocalist [[Siouxsie Sioux]] and bassist [[Steven Severin]]. ''[[The Times]]'' called them "one of the most audacious and uncompromising musical adventurers of the [[post-punk]] era".

Initially associated with the [[punk rock|punk]] scene, the band – including guitarist [[John McKay (guitarist)|John McKay]] and drummer [[Kenny Morris  (drummer)|Kenny Morris]] – rapidly evolved to create "a form of post-punk discord full of daring rhythmic and sonic experimentation". Their debut single "[[Hong Kong Garden (song)|Hong Kong Garden]]" (1978) became a high-charting release peaking at number seven in the [[UK Singles chart]]. Their debut album ''[[The Scream (album)|The Scream]]'' released soon after was met with widespread critical acclaim. Following membership changes, including the addition of guitarist [[John McGeoch]] and drummer [[Budgie (musician)|Budgie]], they changed their musical direction and became one of the most successful [[alternative pop]] groups of the 1980s. Their third album ''[[Kaleidoscope (Siouxsie and the Banshees album)|Kaleidoscope]]'' (1980) peaked at number 5 on the [[UK Albums Chart]]. With ''[[Juju (Siouxsie and the Banshees album)|Juju]]'' (1981) which also reached the top 10, they became an influence on the emerging [[Gothic rock|gothic]] scene.

The band made a breakthrough in North America with the multifaceted album ''[[Peepshow (album)|Peepshow]]'' (1988), which received critical praise. With substantial support from [[alternative rock]] radio stations, they achieved a mainstream hit in the US in 1991 with the pop single "[[Kiss Them for Me (song)|Kiss Them for Me]]". Siouxsie and the Banshees's other best-known songs include "[[Happy House]]" (1980), "[[Spellbound (Siouxsie and the Banshees song)|Spellbound]]" (1981), "[[Cities in Dust]]" (1985) and "[[Peek-a-Boo (Siouxsie and the Banshees song)|Peek-a-Boo]]" (1988). During their career, Siouxsie and the Banshees released 11 studio albums and 30 singles. The band experienced several line-up changes, with Siouxsie and Severin being the only constant members. They disbanded in 1996.

The band were post-punk pioneers. They have been cited as an influence by bands such as [[Joy Division]], [[the Cure]], [[U2]] and [[Radiohead]], [[Tricky (rapper)|Tricky]] and [[Jeff Buckley]].
